run.question:
I'm connected to the ci-cd cluster. We got a P1 alert and need help finding the root cause.
Our cluster inventory is in the app-235-cluster-inventory index and deployment/change history
is in the app-235-change-history index. Please search these indices to investigate.
[
  {
    "annotations": {
      "description": "Online Devices count gradual decrease over 8 hours in [clientorg-alpha] [56%] for over 30m",
      "workload": "clientorg-alpha"
    },
    "fingerprint": "xx1234567890abcd",
    "labels": {
      "alertname": "onlineDevicesCountGradualDecrease",
      "app": "lambda-dashboard-monitoring",
      "cluster": "us-prod-eks",
      "grafana_dashboard_name": "Production-Performance-Overview",
      "org": "clientorg-alpha",
      "severity": "critical",
      "slack_channel": "sre-alerts-channel"
    },
    "startsAt": "30 minutes ago",
    "status": "firing"
  }
]
The alert started right after a deployment. Can you check what's the root cause?

report.summary: The P1 alert (onlineDevicesCountGradualDecrease, org clientorg-alpha, cluster us-prod-eks, app lambda-dashboard-monitoring) could not be tied to anything in this environment. The connected cluster is a kind lab whose only application workloads are namespace app-162 (payments-service, signup-service) and namespace otel-demo. Neither the alert's workload (clientorg-alpha), its app (lambda-dashboard-monitoring) nor its cluster (us-prod-eks) appears in the namespace, deployment, service or node lists, and the two indices the user pointed at describe cluster ci-cd workloads (gitlab-runner, jenkins, argocd-server in namespace ci) that do not exist in the connected cluster. In the change-history index the newest record is 2026-11-22T07:35:43Z (gitlab-runner scale 2->3), i.e. about 90 minutes before the alert's approximate start (~09:05:56Z), so the premise 'the alert started right after a deployment' is not supported by the available change records. Separately, one real failure is visible and is evidenced by the failing workloads' own logs: both pods of app-162 signup-service are not Ready because payments-service is not Ready, and payments-service reports at startup that STRIPE_API_KEY is set to an invalid test key, failing /ready and /health with 'Invalid Stripe API key' (its readiness endpoint returns 503, its Service has no ready endpoints). That failure originates from the credential the payments-service pod reads from Secret app-162/payments-secrets (key stripe-api-key); the secret itself cannot be read, so its value and the change that placed it there are unverified, and nothing in this run links it to the clientorg-alpha alert. Prometheus and Jaeger were unavailable for the whole run (SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE), so no error-rate, latency, trace or alert-rule evidence could be obtained.

claims.text: Inside the authorized window the app-235-cluster-inventory index returned three documents, all for cluster ci-cd in namespace ci: gitlab-runner (image gitlab/gitlab-runner:v16.7.0, replicas 3, status Running, last_updated 2026-11-22T07:35:43Z), jenkins (jenkins/jenkins:2.426.3-lts, replicas 1, Running, 2026-11-22T03:35:43Z) and argocd-server (quay.io/argoproj/argocd:v2.9.3, replicas 2, Running, 2026-11-22T03:35:43Z).

Inside the authorized window the app-235-change-history index returned three change records: BUILD-7X4Q9M, jenkins deployment 2.426.2-lts -> 2.426.3-lts at 2026-11-22T03:35:43Z; BUILD-3NR8Y1, argocd-server deployment v2.9.2 -> v2.9.3 ('ArgoCD security patch update') at 2026-11-22T04:35:43Z; BUILD-5PW2K6, gitlab-runner scale 2 -> 3 replicas at 2026-11-22T07:35:43Z. The newest record is about 2 hours before the query window end (09:35:56Z) and about 90 minutes before the alert's approximate start of ~09:05:56Z derived from startsAt '30 minutes ago'.

The connected cluster has no namespace ci and no Deployments named gitlab-runner, jenkins or argocd-server; its namespaces are app-162, default, kube-node-lease, kube-public, kube-system, local-path-storage, opspilot-readonly and otel-demo, and its 26 Deployments live only in app-162, kube-system, local-path-storage and otel-demo.

Nothing carrying the alert's identities is present in the connected cluster: the only Node is opspilot-m1-control-plane, the only Services are kubernetes/kube-dns/metrics-server plus app-162 (payments-service, signup-service) and the otel-demo services, and no workload, service or namespace named clientorg-alpha or lambda-dashboard-monitoring was returned.

In namespace app-162 the pods payments-service-6d94c44fdc-jwmsq, signup-service-7c89545dc9-85t8h and signup-service-7c89545dc9-gtkx7 are phase Running but Ready=False with reason ContainersNotReady, restartCount 0 and containers started 2026-11-22T09:35:40Z; the Deployments payments-service (revision 1, generation 1) and signup-service report Available=False reason MinimumReplicasUnavailable with unavailableReplicas 1 and 2 respectively.

payments-service-6d94c44fdc-jwmsq logs the exact diagnostic 'ERROR - STRIPE_API_KEY is set to invalid test key - service will fail' at 09:35:42Z, then answers the readiness probe 'GET /ready' with 503 and the liveness probe 'GET /health' with 503, logging 'ERROR - Health check failed: Invalid Stripe API key'.

The payments-service container takes STRIPE_API_KEY from secretKeyRef name payments-secrets key stripe-api-key, and its read-only /app volume app-code is also a secret volume for payments-secrets (signup-service uses signup-secrets in the same way); the secret contents were not readable in this run.

Both signup-service pods log 'ERROR - Payments service check failed: <urlopen error [Errno 111] Connection refused>' and answer 'GET /ready' with 503 between 09:35:45Z and 09:35:55Z; their env sets PAYMENTS_SERVICE_URL=http://payments-service:8080.
The Endpoints objects payments-service and signup-service in app-162 contain only notReadyAddresses (10.244.0.42, 10.244.0.40, 10.244.0.41), so neither Service currently has a ready backend address.

Every long-running container in the cluster records a previous instance terminated with exitCode 255, reason Unknown, finishedAt 2026-11-22T08:04:13Z (including coredns, kube-apiserver, kube-proxy and all otel-demo app containers; kube-state-metrics exitCode 2 with 4 restarts, prometheus-readonly-proxy exitCode 1 with 6 restarts), i.e. a cluster-wide container termination around 08:04:13Z, before the alert's approximate start.

The only events in the window are for app-162: Deployment/payments-service and Deployment/signup-service ScalingReplicaSet 0->1 and 0->2 at 09:35:39Z, three Pods Created/Pulled/Started at 09:35:40Z, plus Warning FailedToCreateEndpoint for app-162/signup-service at 09:32:52Z ('endpoints "signup-service" already exists') and for app-95/orca at 09:21:00Z.

Node opspilot-m1-control-plane is Ready=True and reports MemoryPressure=False, DiskPressure=False and PIDPressure=False, so node readiness and node-level resource pressure do not explain the app-162 pod unreadiness; the cause is visible in the applications' own error logs instead.

A crash-loop, OOM or failed rollout is not the mechanism behind the app-162 unavailability: the containers are running with restartCount 0 and no previous instance, the Deployments are at generation 1 / revision 1, no Evicted/OOMKilled/BackOff event exists, and the failure is reported by the application itself ('Invalid Stripe API key') from its first start.

The invalid credential most likely resides in Secret app-162/payments-secrets under key stripe-api-key, the only source the payments-service pod reads STRIPE_API_KEY from; the secret is unreadable in this run, so the value, its author and the change that introduced it are unverified.

The clientorg-alpha / us-prod-eks alert is not explainable from this environment: nothing here carries that workload, org, app or cluster identity, and no change record falls within 30 minutes of the alert's approximate start, so a 'deployment caused the alert' link is unverified rather than established.

The argocd-server v2.9.3 security patch (BUILD-3NR8Y1, 2026-11-22T04:35:43Z) is worth checking if the P1 concerns Argo CD-managed deployments, but this run produced no evidence tying it to the alert and no argocd-server workload exists in the connected cluster to inspect.

Verify the value of Secret app-162/payments-secrets key stripe-api-key against a valid Stripe test key (and check the items exposed as the /app volume), then re-check payments-service readiness and the signup-service dependency; this is the only verified fault in this cluster and it is demonstrably caused by that credential.

To assess the P1 itself, get access to cluster us-prod-eks and to the clientorg-alpha workloads and their change history around 09:05Z, and check the onlineDevicesCount metric and the Grafana Production-Performance-Overview dashboard there; additionally restore the Prometheus and Jaeger data paths for this environment so error-rate, latency and trace evidence is available.

gaps: Prometheus and Jaeger were unreachable for the entire run: list_prometheus_rules, get_metric_names, get_series, get_all_labels, execute_prometheus_instant_query, get_prometheus_target, traces_list_services and traces_search all returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE (status error, not citable), so no error-rate, latency, trace, kube-state-metrics or alert-rule evidence exists in this report; 'onlineDevices'-type metrics were never observable.

The alert's own scope is outside this environment: cluster us-prod-eks, workload clientorg-alpha and app lambda-dashboard-monitoring do not appear in any namespace, deployment, service, node or index document returned, so the alert's cause cannot be confirmed or excluded here.

A cluster-wide container termination at 2026-11-22T08:04:13Z (exitCode 255, reason Unknown, plus metrics-server/local-path-provisioner/kube-state-metrics exit codes 1-2) is visible on every long-running container; the trigger was not identified in this run and it is not tied to the P1 alert or to the app-162 failure.

The app-162 Deployments carry creationTimestamp 2026-11-22T09:35:39Z, about 17 seconds before the query window end, with revision 1 / generation 1, which matches when this lab environment appears to have been (re)created; their creation time is therefore unreliable as evidence of a real deployment during the incident.

Secret app-162/payments-secrets (and signup-secrets) cannot be read, so the invalid stripe-api-key value, its author and the change that set it remain unverified; the payments_service.py code mounted from that secret was also not inspected.

Queries for networkpolicies (ff5e9465-091d-4728-946e-b381c2dda18e-t0:d12843d5-2f67-4cd7-b423-0074b7f99720), resourcequotas (ff5e9465-091d-4728-946e-b381c2dda18e-t1:80eeaff5-cd18-474c-a34e-d7351136c9c6) and ingresses (ff5e9465-091d-4728-946e-b381c2dda18e-t2:cd1625b8-d453-4904-94db-f174084305c6) returned status no_data, so network policy, quota and ingress misconfiguration were not positively excluded; the frontend log query (dd3629d9-5c77-464b-8a53-9cc9569ea2ad-t1:736158ae-7551-42d6-ac18-6476abaee46f) and the prometheus-readonly-proxy log query (4d209630-a977-4770-8a2b-f8d052f9eaca-t0:30d05635-3f6c-46e1-a7f3-e47516d2d6ea) returned no lines, and the checkout error-pattern query (dd3629d9-5c77-464b-8a53-9cc9569ea2ad-t0:f4a82781-797b-409d-a3d7-b387fa149358) matched nothing, so otel-demo application health was only partially checked (frontend unknown).

The cronjobs query (15a369a5-bc1c-4d5b-8f7c-6506031de008-t0:c52a3694-91e1-473f-aa3e-bcb3ca6674af) and the two unfiltered window queries against app-235-cluster-inventory (2bc1417c-a984-4bff-b644-438dad8bb24b-t0:b67e21bb-40c2-4f46-9550-5d1a4e5ce94c) and app-235-change-history (2bc1417c-a984-4bff-b644-438dad8bb24b-t1:7617ef0b-488c-42a5-8ee7-0c7a9fe45354) returned no data for the narrower default window and are not evidence of absence.

Three inventory documents and one change-history document lie outside the authorized window (6 vs 3 inventory docs, 4 vs 3 change docs) and the Elasticsearch time filter cannot be disabled, so their content is unknown.

The Prometheus error-pattern log view 744b86ec-60e1-41d7-a87e-d740d44afc87-t0:910f89df-c85e-4f23-b510-5f84d018f6ec is marked incomplete (limit: newest 30 of 120 matching lines shown), so older Prometheus warnings were not reviewed.

An event at 2026-11-22T09:21:00Z reports 'Failed to create endpoint for service app-95/orca: endpoints "orca" already exists'; namespace app-95 and object orca are not readable now, so that object is an unread gap.

The dedicated change_history integration is listed as not integrated in this Run; change provenance for the app-162 workloads comes only from the Elasticsearch change-history index, which contains no record for them.
The alert's startsAt is relative ('30 minutes ago'), so its start (~2026-11-22T09:05:56Z) is an approximation; no absolute alert timestamp was provided.
next_steps: Read/rotate the stripe-api-key entry in Secret app-162/payments-secrets and confirm whether the payments-service Deployment was intended to use a test key, then watch payments-service /ready and signup-service dependency checks.

Obtain access to cluster us-prod-eks (or its monitoring) and inspect the clientorg-alpha workload, the onlineDevicesCount series and the change history around 2026-11-22T09:05Z to test the 'alert right after a deployment' claim.
Restore or re-register the Prometheus and Jaeger endpoints used by this environment so metrics and traces can confirm error rates and latency instead of only pod logs and events.
Review the 08:04:13Z cluster-wide container termination (kind node/containerd restart) and its relationship to the prometheus-readonly-proxy restart loop.
Clarify the app-95/orca Endpoints conflict with whoever manages that namespace before it recurs.
